title: Remove flags from commands
summary: A rule takes flags out of a file's command, and a later rule's remove cancels an earlier append
prose: The database gives `main.cpp` both `-DBROKEN` and `-include prefix.h`, which the first rule removes, so it compiles. For `other.cpp` the second rule appends `-DFEATURE` and the third removes it again.

files.text:
[[rules]]
patterns = ["main.cpp"]
remove = ["-DBROKEN", "-include", "prefix.h"]

[[rules]]
patterns = ["other.cpp"]
append = ["-DFEATURE"]

[[rules]]
patterns = ["other.cpp"]
remove = ["-DFEATURE"]

#ifdef BROKEN
#error BROKEN came through
#endif
#ifndef KEPT
#error missing KEPT
#endif
int main() { return 0; }

#ifndef FEATURE
#error missing FEATURE
#endif
int other() { return 0; }
